business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bonded Warehouse Wholesale Trade of Aged Scotch and Bordeaux Wines

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 (as amended), ss.1 (officer definitions), ss.13-19 (incorporation), s.23 (registered office), s.30 (records/financial year), s.40 (consideration for shares), s.50 (securities register), s.66 (directors), s.69 (director disqualification); Companies Regulations 2011 (GN R351 of 26 April 2011)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) filed together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (standard Form CoR 14.2 or customised MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a private (Pty) Ltd; shares must be authorised under the MOI and consideration per s.40 of the Companies Act must satisfy the solvency and liquidity test at allotment; no escrow deposit or pre-incorporation bank account is mandated by South African law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION of ZA (PTY) LTD (Reg. 2025/XXXXXX/07) — It is RESOLVED that: (1) the registered Memorandum of Incorporation be adopted; (2) the subscriber allotment of 1,000 ordinary shares of R1.00 each be confirmed fully paid; (3) the registered office at [Sandton, Johannesburg] be adopted as statutory seat; (4) [Director] be appointed sole Director (s.66), [CFO] Chief Financial Officer (officer, s.1), and [Secretary] Company Secretary; (5) Directors be authorised to open corporate bank accounts and execute SARB exchange-control documents; (6) management be directed to file beneficial-ownership returns, SARS registrations, customs bonded-warehouse, and liquor-licence applications. Dated: ___.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal — 'Name and Company Reservations' (www.cipc.co.za / b2b.cipc.co.za)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Electronically submit Form CoR 9.1 with up to four proposed names. CIPC's name-verification engine checks availability, similarity and offensive-word filters. On approval the name is reserved for 6 months; the reserved name must be consumed by filing the Notice of Incorporation before expiry.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 9.1 (Application for Reservation of a Company Name)
Certified copies of directors' identity documents or passports
CIPC name-analysis report
Proof of payment of CIPC name-reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused or objected to, file a revised name application with CIPC within 30 days; alternatively request a Companies Tribunal name-objection hearing within 20 business days of the refusal notification (s.160 of the Companies Act); re-file with a fresh list of proposed names.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Pre-Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC-accredited incorporation practitioner or notary (pre-filing lodgement prepared for CIPC e-Services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct an accredited attorney or incorporator to draft the MOI (Form CoR 14.2 or customised). Verify each proposed director's eligibility under s.69 (no delinquency, disqualification or prohibited-person status). Subscribers sign the CoR 14.1 and MOI; each director signs CoR 14.3 consent. The MOI must set out authorised share classes, director quorum and powers, and the initial registered office address.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.2 or customised)
Form CoR 14.3 (Consent to act as Director) for each proposed director
Certified identity/passport copies and SARS tax numbers of directors
KYC information of ultimate beneficial owners
Written confirmation of the proposed registered office (not a post-box)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC pre-screening flags a similar name or defective clause, amend the MOI and re-lodge within 10 days; if name conflicts persist, incorporate as a numbered company under the reserved registration number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Payment of Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the completed CoR 14.1, MOI and CoR 14.3 consents into the CIPC portal; pay approximately ZAR 175 (USD 10) via EFT, credit card or instant payment; CIPC adjudicates and issues the COR 14.1A Registration Certificate with a unique registration number (format 2025/XXXXXX/07); the MOI becomes legally binding upon registration.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation) signed by all subscribers
Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.2 or customised)
Forms CoR 14.3 signed consents of directors
Certified IDs/passports of directors and subscribers
Proof of payment of CIPC registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a deferral notice, respond through the CIPC 'List of Consideration' case-management service within 30 days; if the deferral relates to director disqualification or name conflict, file corrected instruments or appeal to the Companies Tribunal under s.159 within 20 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, UIF, Skills and Beneficial-Ownership Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SARS eFiling (www.sarsefiling.co.za); Department of Employment and Labour (UIF); Compensation Fund; CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company at SARS for income tax (Form IT); apply for VAT (Form VAT101) if taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 1 million or elect voluntary registration; register as employer (Form EMP101) for PAYE, UIF and SDL; file with CIPC the CoR 50.1 beneficial-ownership return and maintain the CoR 50.2 securities register; obtain a SARS tax-compliance status certificate; open a corporate bank account with FICA-compliant documents.
required_dossiers: COR 14.1A Registration Certificate
Memorandum of Incorporation
SARS Form IT (Income Tax Registration)
Form VAT101 where applicable
Form EMP101 (PAYE/UIF/SDL)
CoR 50.1 Beneficial-Ownership Information Return
CoR 50.2 Securities Register
BBBEE sworn affidavit (s.13(g), B-BBEE Act 53 of 2003)
Certified director IDs/passports and proof of residential address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS queries incomplete KYC data, furnish outstanding declarations via 'SARS Query' within 30 days; if UIF registration fails on bank validation, obtain automated clearing-house (ACH) verification and re-register; a CIPC beneficial-ownership rejection is cured by amending CoR 50.1 and resubmitting within 30 days without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bonded Warehouse Customs Licence and Liquor Wholesale Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SARS Customs and Excise — Customs Client Office (Bond & Licensing); Gauteng Liquor Board (provincial wholesale liquor licence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to SARS for a Customs and Excise warehouse licence under s.60 of the Customs and Excise Act 91 of 1964 using Form DA10, furnishing a customs bond or SARS-approved surety covering deferred duty, certified warehouse floor plans, stock-accounting system confirmation and tax-compliance status. Simultaneously file a Wholesale Liquor Licence application with the Gauteng Liquor Board under the Gauteng Liquor Act 2 of 2003, including zoning approval, locality plan and police clearance. For aged Scotch and Bordeaux imports, obtain an import permit from DALRRD under the Agricultural Product Standards Act 119 of 1990 and confirm ITAC permit requirements under the International Trade Administration Act 71 of 2002.
required_dossiers: Customs and Excise Form DA10 (Warehouse licence application)
SARS-approved customs bond/surety for deferred duty
COR 14.1A and Memorandum of Incorporation
Lease agreement or title deed of bonded premises
Certified floor plan and structural load certificate (SANS 10160)
Zoning certificate and municipal land-use approval
Gauteng Wholesale Liquor Licence application and locality plan
Fire safety certificate (SANS 10400-T) and emergency plan
Environmental screening/Basic Assessment approval (if triggered)
SARS tax-compliance status certificate (CSD e-Production)
Import permits (DALRRD/ITAC) for wine and spirit consignments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS refuses the warehouse licence for insufficient security or premises non-compliance, increase the bond amount, obtain corrected engineering certification and re-submit to the Customs Client Office; lodge a formal objection and appeal under Chapter 15 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 within 30 days of refusal. If the Gauteng Liquor Board refuses the wholesale licence, file a written appeal to the Gauteng Liquor Board Appeals Committee within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: SARS Customs and Excise (Section 60 Warehouse Licensing Unit) jointly with the Gauteng Liquor Board and the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Customs and Excise Bonded Warehouse Licence (duty-deferred storage of aged Scotch whisky and Bordeaux wines) and Gauteng Wholesale Liquor Licence (Gauteng Liquor Act 2 of 2003)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 — Registration / Basic Assessment: a Basic Assessment Report (BAR) is required only where bonded storage triggers Listing Notice 1 (GN R983 of 2014) activities for hazardous/flammable liquid storage above 80 m³ or where infrastructure is located in a sensitive area; sealed bottled alcoholic beverages in a standard warehouse below the listed thresholds are exempt from mandatory EIA but must be documented in an environmental screening report submitted to the competent authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero liquid discharge from bonded areas: all spirit/barrel storage must be bunded to 110% containment; no spillwater may enter municipal stormwater drains. Sewer-discharged trade effluent must meet municipal limits (pH 6-10, TSS ≤ 500 mg/L, COD ≤ 500 mg/L). VOC losses are limited by the National Ambient Air Quality Standards (GN 1210 of 2009) and the 20 mg/Nm³ VOC general emission limit under GN R922 of 2013; waste spirit containers must be managed by a registered hazardous-waste transporter with manifests under s.31 of the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by Municipal Emergency Services under SANS 10400-T and the National Building Regulations and Building Standards Act 103 of 1977; structural certification of racking and storage loads (SANS 10160); electrical Certificate of Compliance (SANS 10142); Major Hazard Installation notification and HAZOP risk assessment under the OHS Act 85 of 1993 and the Major Hazard Installation Regulations, 2021; Hazardous Chemical Agents compliance (assessment, labelling, medical surveillance) under the HCS Regulations, 2021; Class 3 flammable liquid segregation; occupational clearance attesting the premises are fit for bonded wholesale trade operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — national tax and customs administration; eFiling portal at sarsefiling.co.za; customs electronic declarations via SARS Customs systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Appoint a resident public officer/representative and register the (Pty) Ltd through SARS eFiling to obtain an Income Tax Reference Number (ITR). Step 2: Register for VAT using VAT101 once taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 or elect voluntary registration where turnover exceeds ZAR 50,000. Step 3: Register as a Customs/Excise client under the Customs Control Act 31 of 2014 and Customs and Excise Act 91 of 1964 to obtain a customs code and bonded warehouse licence for wine/spirits duty suspension. Step 4: Register as an employer for PAYE, UIF, SDL and Skills Development Levy if staff are engaged. Step 5: Record non-resident shareholding; the (Pty) Ltd remains a South African resident taxpayer and non-resident shareholders are subject to Dividends Withholding Tax at source.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not maintain a US-style check-the-box election; entity classification is determined by domestic income tax law. Relevant elections for a qualifying (Pty) Ltd include: Small Business Corporation status (s 12E) for graduated corporate rates; micro business turnover tax election (Sixth Schedule); VAT group registration election (s 50A VAT Act) for connected persons; hybrid instrument and hybrid mismatch adjustments under s 8E, 8F, 8EA and s 8FA–8L; and exchange rate base cost elections under s 24I. Binding private rulings can be obtained under s 76 Tax Administration Act for uncertainty.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, supplemented by the Customs and Excise Act 91 of 1964 and the Customs Control Act 31 of 2014 for excisable wine and spirits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAT registration is triggered where taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period; voluntary registration is available where taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 but do not exceed ZAR 1,000,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently impose a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping framework. VAT tax invoices must comply with s 20 VAT Act requirements for authenticity, integrity and legibility, and electronic invoices are accepted provided complete records are retained for five years. SARS eFiling mandates periodic VAT201 returns, while customs and excise movements require electronic SAD500 export declarations and bonded warehouse stock/transfer reporting through SARS Customs systems. Bonded wine/spirits removals must occur under excise duty control before zero-rated export.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods qualify for zero-rating under s 11(1)(a) VAT Act where the supplier supplies goods for export and the goods are physically removed from South Africa within the prescribed period, normally 90 days from date of supply, subject to SARS extension. Bonded wine/spirits zero-rate only where the goods are entered for export from the bonded warehouse under customs/excise control and the duty suspension is terminated on lawful export. Services qualify under s 11(2) where physically rendered outside South Africa or supplied to non-residents and not used in South Africa, subject to statutory conditions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) accepted by SARS Customs evidencing entry for export from the bonded warehouse
Bill of Lading, airway bill, or road manifest proving physical departure of the goods from South Africa
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank foreign-exchange record confirming export proceeds received in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS audits zero-rated export refunds before payment and may re-characterise the supply as taxable at 15% where export proof is deficient or the statutory export period is breached, raising a retrospective VAT assessment. Additional liabilities include understatement penalties under the Tax Administration Act of up to 200% for intentional non-disclosure, interest at the prescribed rate, and potential criminal prosecution for fraudulent zero-rating claims. Bonded warehouse operators also face forfeiture of goods, cancellation of the bond licence, and retrospective excise duty clawback where wine/spirits are not lawfully exported.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) and Authorised Dealers under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933, and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: ZAR is freely convertible for current account transactions, with only documentary reporting obligations. Capital account inflows and outflows are generally permitted but subject to exchange-control reporting, prescribed limits, and Authorised Dealer intervention. Non-resident profit remittances are permitted upon submission of a SARS tax clearance/pin, B-form or equivalent reporting, proof of lawful dividend declaration, and compliance with the Companies Act, 2008; no prior FinSurv approval is required for ordinary dividend remittances below the current reporting threshold.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Exchange Control Regulation 4, export proceeds must be received by an Authorised Dealer in South Africa within 180 days from the date of export, unless an extension is granted in writing. All export proceeds must be repatriated to and credited in the exporter's local foreign-currency account maintained with a South African Authorised Dealer; however, there is no statutory requirement to convert the proceeds into ZAR. Funds may be held, sold, or applied in accordance with the Authorised Dealer's approved foreign-currency account limits.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Offshore digital EMI licences do not confer a direct right to conduct banking business in South Africa, as deposit-taking and cross-border payment account services are reserved to institutions licensed under the Banks Act, 1990. Legitimate fintechs can only function through partnership/white-label arrangements with a South African Authorised Dealer; full account opening and transaction clearing must ultimately flow through a domestic bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA compels identification, verification, and beneficial-ownership assessment. For a non-resident-owned, Medium-Risk Enhanced bonded-wine business, South African banks generally require at least one authorised director or senior signatory to attend an in-person account-opening interview at the bank's office, with original or notarised corporate documents presented. Fully remote onboarding is occasionally possible for established foreign corporates using apostilled documents and video-verification technology, but physical presence materially increases on-boarding speed and approval probability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership with limited local operational nexus after incorporation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum of Incorporation, shareholders register with UBO details, FICA corporate KYC pack, SARS tax clearance certificate, physical office lease, entity structure chart, passports/government IDs of all directors and 25%+ shareholders, and source-of-funds declaration for the initial capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bonded-warehouse alcohol and spirits classification attracting enhanced due diligence under PEP and high-risk industry screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid SARS Customs and Excise licence (DA185 or current equivalent), bonded warehouse operating permit, written lease or title deed for the licensed premises, Excise duty payment plan / deferred payment arrangement, procurement invoices for wine and spirits, storage and inventory control reports, and third-party audit certificate confirming segregation of bonded goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound transfers from affiliated offshore entities that lack clear purpose codes or loan documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed cross-border facility agreement or equity subscription letter, board resolution authorising the transfer, SARS tax clearance/pin, Authorised Dealer inward notification acknowledgement referencing the B-form or equivalent reporting, company cash-flow forecast, and underlying commercial invoices for stock purchases.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign direct investment must be routed through a designated inward capital account opened with a South African Authorised Dealer. The transfer should be made via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 with a reference to inward investment seasoning and the reporting purpose code; the Authorised Dealer will record the transaction for exchange-control statistical purposes and issue an inward notification acknowledgement (B-form/IMF balance-of-payments reporting). Supporting documents include board resolutions, subscription/financing agreement, UBO identification, and SARS tax clearance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Treasury clears bonded-warehouse purchases, excise settlements, and foreign supplier payments through: SWIFT MT103/MT103 STP for direct cross-border wires; commercial letters of credit issued by a tier-1 South African bank under UCP600; and ZAR-denominated local payments via SAMOS (South African Multiple Option Settlement). For the bonded-warehouse model, domestic excise and customs payments are effected by EFT/RTGS in ZAR, while offshore wine and spirits purchases are settled via LC or MT103 with full trade-document compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts (FECs) with a licensed Authorised Dealer for firm trade receivables and payables
Cross-currency swaps with an Authorised Dealer for medium-term balance-sheet exposure linked to shareholder funding or dividend commitments
Vanilla currency options (within South African option regulations) for selective protection of bonded procurement contracts
Offshore NDFs are not permissible for South African resident entities unless specific SARB approval is obtained and a real trade or interest-rate exposure is demonstrated

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under Section 33(1) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary date of incorporation, as stated on the CIPC notice; ordinarily using ERS online filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC levies a monthly late-penalty fee of ZAR 360; continued non-filing for two consecutive years triggers CIPC administrative strike-off proceedings after a final dere­gistration notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Upsale-Register Lodgment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the annual return; each reportable change in beneficial ownership within 7 business days after filing the internal resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file constitutes an offence under section 14(3) of the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering) Amendment Act; a compliance notice by CIPC may carry a fine up to ZAR 1,000,000 and director liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Preparation and Delivery of Annual Financial Statements (IFRS for SMEs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders (delivered within 6 months after financial year-end; retained in registered office for CIPC/SARS inspection on request)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the company's financial year-end unless an external extension is obtained; annual return remains separate from AFS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be disqualified or personally liable; CIPC may issue a compliance notice and, without rectification, the company may be prohibited from filing annual continuity filings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is required where the Public Interest Score (PIS) exceeds 350; an independent review is required for a PIS between 100 and 349; a company with a PIS below 100 remains exempt unless the MOI or a creditor/shareholder mandates an audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS / IFRS for SMEs (South African local GAAP not applicable); financial statements must be prepared per section 29 of the Companies Act and may be consolidated where the (Pty) Ltd has subsidiaries

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must keep a Beneficial Ownership Register and file a confirmation with CIPC at the same time as the Annual Return; any transfer of shares resulting in a beneficial ownership change must first be recorded in the Register of Members, then lodged with CIPC within 7 business days of the resolution and thereafter confirmed as part of the next annual filing.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 100-200 per year for registered office and company secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500-5,000 for an independent review; USD 6,000-12,000 for a full statutory audit where PIS triggers such requirement

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard corporate rate 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023); no statutory tax holiday; qualifying Small Business Corporations may access graduated rates (0%-27%) and the Employment Tax Incentive. Assessed losses carry forward indefinitely under s 20 ITA, but set-off is capped at ZAR 1,000,000 plus 80% of the excess taxable income for years ending on/after 31 March 2023 (i.e., 0-year fixed limit).
